articles.title: Pill to treat pancreatic cancer hailed as ‘biggest breakthrough in decades’
articles.description: Cancer undetectable for one in 12 patients in daraxonrasib trial, while nearly all participants’ tumours stopped growing A pill that can shrink and potentially eliminate pancreas tumours is being hailed as the biggest breakthrough treatment for the cancer in decades. In one in 12 of the patients given the drug, daraxonrasib, during a trial, the cancer became undetectable, and the tumours stopped growing in almost all of the 61 patients. The trial participants had recently been diagnosed with advanced pancreatic cancer that had spread to other parts of the body. Continue reading...

articles.title: Spacecraft reaches Mercury on second-ever mission to enter its orbit
articles.description: BepiColombo double probe will map planet’s surface and study its interior to shed light on its unusually large core After a voyage of more than eight years and 6bn miles, a joint European-Japanese space mission has arrived at Mercury and is preparing to swing into orbit around the tiny, barely explored world. The BepiColombo mission will become only the second in history to circle the first rock from the sun and the smallest planet in the solar system when flight controllers fire the spacecraft’s thrusters on Saturday and send it into orbit. Continue reading...

articles.title: An elevator, a brick wall and a bathroom: scientists use gravity to send ‘practically unblockable’ message

source.name: Donna Lu Assistant editor, climate, environment and science

articles.description: Australian physicists chose to transmit the word ‘gravity’ in binary code through brick wall Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Australian scientists have used gravity as a means of communication, in a proof-of-concept experiment involving a snail-paced 1950s elevator, a brick wall and a men’s bathroom. Physicists at the University of Queensland have used gravity to transmit a “practically unblockable” message about 70cm through a brick wall, by sending an elevator up and down between two floors and measuring changes in the gravitational field as a result of the movement. Continue reading...

articles.title: Spuds in space: scientists say potatoes could be key food source for future moon base
articles.description: New report details how potatoes were successfully cultivated in simulated lunar soil The humble potato could be the key to sustaining human life on the moon, according to a new scientific report asserting that prolonged lunar exploration will depend on life support systems capable of producing food there. Potatoes are an ideal candidate for farming on the moon, scientists on a project backed by the US space agency Nasa concluded, after they succeeded in growing them in simulated lunar soil. Continue reading...

articles.title: IPCC report delay will threaten global effort to tackle climate crisis, says top scientist

source.name: Fiona Harvey, Graham Readfearn and Damien Gayle in Antalya

articles.description: Johan Rockström, one of world’s leading climate experts, says slowing down scientific work puts cooperation at risk Climate science is “foundational” to the Paris agreement and worldwide progress on tackling global heating, and attempts to delay new scientific reports threaten global cooperation on tackling the crisis, one of the world’s leading climate scientists has warned. Johan Rockström, the director of the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research, said the world’s leading body of climate scientists, the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, must be allowed to work as quickly as possible on its next comprehensive assessment of global knowledge of the climate systems. Continue reading...

articles.title: Could measles and midterms bring down Maha? – podcast

source.name: Presented by Ian Sample, with Jessica Glenza, produced by Ellie Sans, sound design by Joel Cox; the executive producer was Ellie Bury

articles.description: This week the US lost its measles elimination status, an official recognition that the infectious disease is endemic in the country after being eliminated for 26 years. To find out what this means in practical terms for citizens, Ian Sample hears from the Guardian US health reporter Jessica Glenza. She explains why it comes at an already difficult time for the health secretary, Robert F Kennedy Jr, and his Make America Healthy Again movement, and what newly elected Democrats will be focusing on when it comes to health Clips: CBS, NBC, CBC US loses measles elimination status amid worst outbreak since 1991 Continue reading...

articles.title: ‘Remarkable luck’: wreck of first Australian-built warship discovered exactly 128 years after sinking
articles.description: HMCS Spitfire was commissioned by colonial government to protect against Russian warships during the Crimean war The wreck of Australia’s first locally built warship has been discovered 128 years after sinking off the coast of far north Queensland. Marine archaeologists found the remains of Ex HMCS Spitfire on 21 August, the anniversary of its sinking in 1898. Continue reading...

articles.title: Senate committee rejects Trump nominee to lead National Science Foundation
articles.description: Committee chair Bill Cassidy, a Republican, said Jim O’Neill ‘did not do enough to stand up for science’ in previous posts Jim O’Neill will not undergo a confirmation hearing on Wednesday to head he National Science Foundation (NSF) because he “did not do enough to stand up for science” in his previous position, said Bill Cassidy, a Republican from Louisiana who is chair of the Senate committee on health, education, labor and pensions. This ends O’Neill’s run for the top US scientific organization, an embattled independent federal agency that has seen major budget cuts and grant freezes under the Trump administration. The next NSF nominee will face a Democratic-led Senate. Continue reading...

articles.title: Pill to treat pancreatic cancer hailed as ‘biggest breakthrough in decades’
articles.description: Cancer undetectable for one in 12 patients in daraxonrasib trial, while nearly all participants’ tumours stopped growing A pill that can shrink and potentially eliminate pancreas tumours is being hailed as the biggest breakthrough treatment for the cancer in decades. In one in 12 of the patients given the drug, daraxonrasib, during a trial, the cancer became undetectable, and the tumours stopped growing in almost all of the 61 patients. The trial participants had recently been diagnosed with advanced pancreatic cancer that had spread to other parts of the body. Continue reading...

articles.title: Spacecraft reaches Mercury on second-ever mission to enter its orbit
articles.description: BepiColombo double probe will map planet’s surface and study its interior to shed light on its unusually large core After a voyage of more than eight years and 6bn miles, a joint European-Japanese space mission has arrived at Mercury and is preparing to swing into orbit around the tiny, barely explored world. The BepiColombo mission will become only the second in history to circle the first rock from the sun and the smallest planet in the solar system when flight controllers fire the spacecraft’s thrusters on Saturday and send it into orbit. Continue reading...
